subject: Computer Networking
title: Google Cloud's Network Outage (2019)
description: A fast breakdown of Google Cloud's Network Outage (2019) for builders.

hook.text: On June 2, 2019, Google Cloud lost connectivity for four hours. YouTube, Gmail, and Snapchat all went down.

buildup.text: A network config change meant for a few servers was accidentally applied to a much larger region.

discovery.text: The misconfig caused massive packet loss. Services on Google's network degraded or failed entirely.

twist.text: Many third-party services also run on Google Cloud. One outage cascaded across the whole internet.

climax.text: Google published a detailed post-mortem and added guardrails against wide-scope config changes.

punchline.text: A config meant for a few servers hit a whole region. Scope matters.

quiz.question: Why did Google Cloud's 2019 outage affect non-Google services?
options: Many third-party services run on Google Cloud infrastructure
Google's DNS servers serve the entire internet
The outage physically damaged other companies' cables

details.summary: In June 2019, a network configuration error at Google Cloud caused a four-hour outage affecting Google Cloud Platform, YouTube, Gmail, and Snapchat. The misconfiguration caused network congestion that cascaded across multiple regions and services.
details.whyItMatters: Even Google, with its world-class engineering, suffers outages from configuration errors. Complexity makes all large networks vulnerable regardless of the operator's skill.
takeaways: A configuration error caused cascading network congestion
Multiple Google services were affected for four hours
Third-party services on Google Cloud were also impacted

faq.question: What caused the Google Cloud network outage?
faq.answer: A configuration change intended for a small number of servers was accidentally applied broadly, causing a massive traffic shift. The resulting congestion overwhelmed network links, and the cascading effects spread across regions and services for four hours.

faq.question: How did Google respond to the incident?
faq.answer: Google published a detailed post-mortem, improved configuration change validation processes, and added automated canary testing for network changes. They also improved monitoring to detect unexpected traffic patterns earlier before they cascade.
